question:
A 46-year-old male presents with a one-month history of increased urinary frequency and terminal
hematuria. He emigrated from Kenya to the United States five years ago. He denies smoking, alcohol
consumption, or illicit drug use. Physical examination reveals splenomegaly and a palpable liver edge.
Urine dipstick testing is strongly positive for blood. Pelvic CT imaging shows bladder wall thickening
and fibrosis. Bladder biopsy obtained during cystoscopy confirms squamous cell carcinoma. Which of
the following additional findings is most likely in this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Hydronephrosis due
to ureteral obstruction (B) Nonpitting lower extremity edema (C) Schistosoma eggs in the stool (D)
Hepatic periportal fibrosis (E) Chronic venous stasis changes in the lower extremities (F) Elevated
mean pulmonary artery pressure (G) Increased serum alpha-fetoprotein (H) Peripheral eosinophilia (I)
Calcified cysts in the liver parenchyma (J) Decreased serum albumin levels
 A. Increased serum alpha-fetoprotein
B. Hydronephrosis due to ureteral obstruction
C. Nonpitting lower extremity edema
D. Decreased serum albumin levels
E. Elevated mean pulmonary artery pressure
F. Schistosoma eggs in the stool
G. Calcified cysts in the liver parenchyma
H. Chronic venous stasis changes in the lower extremities
I. Hepatic periportal fibrosis
J. Peripheral eosinophilia
